import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
from pathlib import Path

def task_func(mean=123456.908, std_dev=1.2, save_plots=False):
    """
    Generate a random sample from a normal distribution, compute skewness and kurtosis,
    and optionally save a histogram and QQ plot.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float, list[str]]: (skewness, kurtosis, plot_paths)
    """
    if std_dev < 0:
        raise ValueError("std_dev must be non-negative")

    rng = np.random.default_rng()
    sample_size = 1000
    sample = rng.normal(loc=mean, scale=std_dev, size=sample_size)

    skewness = float(stats.skew(sample, bias=False))
    kurtosis = float(stats.kurtosis(sample, fisher=True, bias=False))

    plot_paths = []
    if save_plots:
        hist_path = Path("normal_histogram.png").resolve()
        qq_path = Path("normal_qq_plot.png").resolve()

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
        ax.hist(sample, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.75, color="steelblue", edgecolor="black")
        ax.set_title("Histogram of Normal Sample")
        ax.set_xlabel("Value")
        ax.set_ylabel("Density")
        fig.tight_layout()
        fig.savefig(hist_path, dpi=150)
        plt.close(fig)

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
        stats.probplot(sample, dist="norm", plot=ax)
        ax.set_title("Normal Q-Q Plot")
        fig.tight_layout()
        fig.savefig(qq_path, dpi=150)
        plt.close(fig)

        plot_paths = [str(hist_path), str(qq_path)]

    return skewness, kurtosis, plot_paths
